Project Quality Management. PM Series - 10 | by Vivek Tiwari | Medium
By Vivek Tiwari
Quality Management — Executing Phase Manage Quality The main focus of this process is to
execute the plan that the project manager and team have created to meet the quality
standards for the product or service.

The criticaloutputsof this process are Quality
Reports— that include information about quality issues with the project, and
recommendation on the improvement of the current process Test and Evaluation Documents— A
checklist used by Quality Assurance teams to measure the quality standards of a product. How do we achieve the desired output?

First, consider analyzing the Quality Management
Plan (QMP) which provides information about the quality standards, objectives, control,
and assurance procedures. In addition to the QMP, project documents such as the Lessons
Learned Register, Quality Metrics, and Risk Report should also be reviewed.

These
documents provide information on recommended methods for improving quality, metrics used
to measure quality, and risks that should be taken into consideration. In addition to the
commonITTOs, consider the below tools as critical to be applied to the above-mentioned
inputs Under the data-gathering process, checklists play a critical role in helping QA
team members review the essential components of the product and ensure that the quality
standards specified in the checklists are met.

Under the data-representation process, the
cause-and-effect diagram is vital which helps the team to identify the cause of the
defect. Quality audits are essential as they ensure that best practices are being followed
and enable the sharing of important audit metrics with stakeholders, keeping them informed
about the end product.

Design for X — that developers use to design a specific part of the
product. By utilizing the above-mentioned processes, standardized quality can be achieved
through effective actions.
